edits.current: "subtype": "Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current: "subtype": "Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Node, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current: "subtype": "Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. C structs use fixed-width scalars, GMP integers and length-aware string/byte spans with explicit ownership; C++ values use fixed-width scalars, boost::multiprecision::cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. C also preserves existing output payloads, tags and ownership on rejection. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current: "subtype": "Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In C/C++, checked fields retain the declared primitive's public host type across all nineteen tested bases. C structs use fixed-width scalars, GMP integers and length-aware string/byte spans with explicit ownership; C++ values use fixed-width scalars, boost::multiprecision::cpp_int, std::string and std::vector<uint8_t>. Unit, Bool, Char, floats and native words keep their ordinary generated representations. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. C also preserves existing output payloads, tags and ownership on rejection. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current: "subtype": "Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

Both author routes and full/result-only APIs reproduce complete CPAN component and runtime archives from two authors. Perl 5.36.3 and 5.38.2, each threaded and unthreaded, install them offline after author removal as prebuilt-only and build-xs deliveries and replay after physical relocation on Linux x64/glibc 2.36 with an explicit 2.36 package floor. The four accepted selections ran serially under two frozen producer revisions and recorded per-run host-load admission ceilings of 6, 8, 8 and 12; the hosted default stays 6 and the disk and memory floors never changed. Original archives, receipts, control runs, preserved non-accepted launches and selected sources at both revisions are retained; external toolchain binaries are not. The Perl caller's check counts equal the Python caller's as a consistency check, not as borrowed evidence. Other hosts need their own primitive-base nominal acceptance. edits.current: "subtype": "Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Perl, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undef for Unit, the generated native boolean for Bool, IV or UV scalars for fixed-width integers and native machine words, Math::BigInt for Nat and Int, NV scalars for Float32 and Float, and strings for String, Char and ByteArray. Generated blessed wrappers carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current: "subtype": "Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Each present Subtype leaf uses the selected checked Lean constructor; accepted normalization reaches the export. A rejected leaf fails the call without changing the input; later valid calls still work. Results expose the proof-backed base values. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In Python, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: None for Unit, bool for Bool, int for every integer and native machine word, float for Float32 and Float, str for String and Char, and bytes for ByteArray. Generated frozen dataclasses carry the record and variant fields. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current: "subtype": "Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. In C#, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: Unit, bool, byte, ushort, uint, ulong, sbyte, short, int, long, BigInteger for Nat and Int, float, double, string, byte[], Rune, ulong for USize and long for ISize. Generated sealed records and cases carry the record and active-variant fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves the complete caller value and later valid calls succeed. edits.current: "subtype": "In Java and Kotlin, checked nominal fields preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations with 64-bit machine words: the generated Unit singleton, boolean, int for UInt8 and UInt16, long for UInt32, BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize, byte, short, int and long for the signed fixed-width integers, long for ISize, float and double including signed zero, String, byte[] for ByteArray and int Unicode scalars for Char. Generated records and sealed variant cases carry the payloads without proof fields; the Lean Pair record is renamed PacketPair to avoid the generated tuple class. Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

Host conversions reject out-of-range unsigned values, negative Nat values, surrogate characters, invalid UTF-16 text and null payloads before Lean runs. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record. Copied results project existing Lean values without selecting or running an input constructor. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor."

edits.current: "subtype": "In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\\Math\\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current: "subtype": "In native PHP, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations: null for Unit; bool; int for the bounded integers through UInt32 and Int64; Brick\\Math\\BigInteger for UInt64, Nat, Int and USize; float for Float32 and Float64; string for String and Char; Bytes for ByteArray; and int for 64-bit ISize. Generated final readonly classes carry record and active-variant fields without proof fields. Each input site retains its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Fixed-width overflow, invalid Unicode scalars, malformed Bytes, non-finite floats where the contract refuses them, wrong classes and invalid Fin siblings reject before Lean dispatch. Rejection preserves the complete caller value, including signed zero and embedded NUL data, and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project proof-backed payloads without input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current:
"The installed generic-Subtype matrix covers the closed GenericNat alias of GenericCarrier Nat, its Positive field, retained Nat marker, distinct plusOne and plusTwo per-specialization constructor choices, and constructor-free copied results. It does not expose open generic host types, arbitrary type arguments or predicates, generic Fin fields, PHP-Wasm, callbacks, ownership, recursive generic graphs, dispatch cost or peak memory. The dependent foundation separately checks retained Nat, Bool and String indices in compiler and reviewed contracts; it does not infer installed host coverage for those dependent shapes. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs.",
        "Owned Subtype acceptance covers one selected Nat Subtype field in the tested acyclic Bundle, borrowed and transferred inputs, leased or retained results, rejection before ownership movement, exact cleanup and recovery through the named public package APIs. Recursive owned graphs, owned checked-record fields, owned callback positions, arbitrary predicates, dispatch cost and peak memory remain separate work. PHP-Wasm has separate owned-Subtype evidence and is not widened by this promotion. External runtimes, compilers, package managers and operating-system distributions remain trusted recorded inputs."

edits.current: "subtype": "In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current: "subtype": "In WIT, checked nominal values preserve all nineteen tested primitive representations through the Component Model adapter and its 64-bit native Lean host: the unit enum for Unit; bool; u8, u16, u32 and u64; s8, s16, s32 and s64; exact little-endian `list<u32>` limbs for Nat; a record of sign and limbs for Int; f32 and f64 including signed zero; string with embedded NUL; `list<u8>` for ByteArray; char as a Unicode scalar; and u64/s64 for USize/ISize. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor, including distinct normalizing choices for the same record, fixed-width wrapping, float negation, text and byte extension and the tested character replacement. The host rejects wrong kinds, malformed fields, non-canonical limbs, negative zero, surrogates and invalid UTF-8 before Lean runs. Rejected refinements leave caller values unchanged; a later valid call succeeds. Copied results project existing Lean values and require no input constructor selection. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."

edits.current: "subtype": "Pass the primitive base value, including inside Array, List, Option, Prod and Except containers using their generated host representations. Transparent aliases and the tested closed List specialization keep their constructor choices. In browser pages, React and workers, checked fields retain the declared primitive's host representation across all nineteen tested bases: undefined (void in TypeScript) for Unit, boolean for Bool, bigint for UInt64, Int64, Nat and Int, string for String and Char, Uint8Array for ByteArray, and number for the other fixed-width integers, floats and wasm32 machine words. Each input site keeps its selected checked constructor and accepted normalization; only the active variant branch is checked. Rejection preserves caller values and later valid calls succeed. Copied results project existing Lean payloads without proof fields or input constructor selections, including standalone result-only packages. GenericNat is the concrete GenericCarrier Nat alias: its value field crosses without a proof, each named specialization retains its selected plusOne or plusTwo constructor, and copied results carry no constructor. In the tested acyclic owned Bundle, the selected constructor validates the checked field before a successful transferred-input handoff; rejection leaves ownership unchanged, and later valid calls recover."
